title: Data Oblivious CPU: Microarchitectural Side-channel Leakage-Resilient Processor
problem: Microarchitectural side-channel attacks (cache timing, speculative execution) remain broadly applicable despite various targeted defenses; current approaches are narrowly tailored, leaving systems exposed to diverse attack vectors.
motivation: Security-critical systems require defense against the full spectrum of microarchitectural side-channels; generic approaches that minimize performance overhead while providing broad protection are essential.
method: Dynamic instruction decoding strategy that selectively decodes instructions into secure (side-channel resilient) or performance versions based on the sensitivity of data being processed. Non-sensitive data path uses optimized performance instructions; sensitive data path uses secure variants. Implemented on RISC-V BOOM out-of-order processor.
key_novelty: Generic data-aware dynamic decoding mechanism that provides selective side-channel resilience with minimal architectural changes and zero overhead for non-sensitive workloads.
contributions: Up to 25% overhead for security-critical workloads
Scalable and efficient solution for broad side-channel defense

metrics.other: 2% FPGA resource overhead, 0% overhead unprotected, 25% overhead protected

limitations: Evaluation on RISC-V BOOM; applicability to other ISAs and processor microarchitectures (out-of-order vs. in-order) not thoroughly explored.
primary_theme: Data-aware dynamic decoding for generic side-channel resilience
